texts: good. the date, the beginning, the thirty-night solo stretch (marked solo, thirty nights long) and the Harbor Station all land, and the stretch becomes the referent the four 'during the solo stretch' sentences hang on. One thing you need not act on: 'began a <noun>' sits outside the rule written for 'began to V' / 'began V-ing', so the stretch was marked ongoing but never past -- our omission, not your wording.

good. the whole accompanying -- Pell as the one accompanying, Coraline Ash as the one accompanied, the stretch it would have fallen inside, and past tense -- is denied as a single unit, which is exactly right.

bad: 'her own' vanished -- the off-nights went in as a bare time word with nothing tying them to Pell, so the parse now says Pell visited on off-nights in general, and the several visits collapse into one. A possessed plural noun phrase has no slot in the time role, so the fix is to make it a clause, which is covered as a recurrence rule: 'Whenever Pell had a night off, she visited the Harbor Station.'

mixed: the agent, the lantern, sundown, the link to the solo stretch and the tense are all right; only 'every night' is mis-filed, because 'night' is a time-of-day word like 'morning', not a cycle length our time vocabulary defines. State the cycle in days and the sundown slot stays clean: 'During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash lit the lantern at sundown every day.'

mixed: the mire-essence (with its essence genus), the midnight time point, the link to the solo stretch and the tense are all right; only 'every night' is mis-filed, since 'night' is a time-of-day word, not a cycle length. Same repair: 'During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash refreshed the mire-essence at midnight every day.'

mixed: the wick, the third watch, the link to the solo stretch and the tense all land; only 'every night' is mis-filed, for the same reason as the other nightly sentences. Same repair: 'During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash trimmed the wick at the third watch every day.'

mixed: the same single problem as the other nightly sentences -- 'night' is a time-of-day word, not a cycle length -- and here it also collides with the stated time point, since the by-the-book repair would add 'night' as a second time on an event you have already placed at dawn. Saying the cycle in days removes both at once: 'During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash extinguished the lantern at dawn every day.'
good. the keeping, the notebook and the careful manner all land, with the adverb kept in its own surface form.
